To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SV40-induced transformation of normal human fibroblasts requires the pRb binding region of LTAg.
the LTAg regions responsible for binding the Rb and p53 proteins play different roles in the transformation of NHDFs and LFS fibroblasts.

the SV40 large tumor antigen has two distinct activities: (a) the p110Rb binding region is required for focus formation and (b) loss of normal p 53 function is required for increased proliferative potential.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of p53 in the senescence and transformation processes.
the molecular mechanisms that control cell proliferation and differentiation in normal cells.
the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying the transformation process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53 function is more important in the process of senescence, whereas the RB function is more important for cell cycle progression.
the SV40 large tumor antigen is a multifunctional protein which can bind to the p53 and the Rb protein.

SV40-induced transformation in NHDFs is enhanced by loss p53 function, and that the LTAg p53-binding region is required to induce focus formation, and the LTAg pRB-binding region is required for the maintenance of transformed phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the p53 gene is a tumor suppressor gene that is involved in the control of the cell cycle.
SV40-induced transformation of NHDFs requires p110Rb binding and is enhanced by p53 loss, whereas transformation of LFS fibroblasts requires p53 loss and is enhanced by the p110Rb region.

the SV40 T antigen can induce focus formation in normal human diploid cells by binding to the pRb protein, but that the loss of normal p 53 function is required to induce a permanent increase in proliferative potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p110Rb binding is necessary for the SV40-induced transformation of NHDFs, but is not sufficient.
p53 and Rb have different roles in the regulation of the proliferative life span of human cells.
the p53 pathway is more important in the control of human cell proliferation than the pRB pathway.
